svg.title: Allied Four-Zone Occupation of Germany and Four-Sector Berlin (1945)
svg.desc: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History map showing the 1945 division of defeated Germany into British (north-west), French (south-west), US (south and Bremen), and Soviet (east) occupation zones, Poland's westward border shift to the Oder–Neisse line, and a magnified inset of Four-Sector Berlin located 100 miles deep inside the Soviet Zone.

g.text: Potsdam: Each power takes from own zone.
100 Miles Deep Inside the Soviet Occupation Zone
Western road, rail & air access to West Berlin depended on
Ex-German Lands Placed Under Polish Rule (1945)
Stalin backed Communist Lublin Poles vs democratic London Poles.
EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · OPTION P4: YALTA & POTSDAM CONFERENCES
Allied Occupation Zones of Germany & Four-Sector Berlin (1945)
EDEXCEL EXAM TAKEAWAY · WHY 1945 DIVISION BUILT FUTURE COLD WAR CRISES
Agreed at Yalta (Feb 1945) and confirmed at Potsdam (July–Aug 1945), dividing Germany and Berlin into four zones left
Western-held West Berlin stranded 100 miles inside Soviet territory while zone-by-zone reparations split East and West economically.
